transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Right, let's get going. Three things on the list today: the offline sync approach, the crash rate, and when we actually ship this.

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: Can I start with sync? Because it affects the other two.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: So we prototyped both. The delta-based approach is faster on paper but it falls apart when a device has been offline for more than a week. We hit conflicts we can't resolve automatically. The full-snapshot approach is heavier on bandwidth but it's predictable.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: How much heavier?

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: About four times the payload on a typical account. Call it two megabytes instead of five hundred kilobytes.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's fine on wifi. It's not fine on a train.

transcript.speaker: Luca Bertolini
transcript.text: Most of our sync events happen when people open the app in the morning, and that's overwhelmingly on wifi. I pulled the numbers last week.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Then let's go with full snapshot. I'd rather have something that works badly on a train than something that corrupts data after a holiday. That's decided.

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: Agreed. I'll take that.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Owen, can you have the full-snapshot implementation in review by the twenty-fourth of September?

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: Twenty-fourth of September, yes. It's mostly plumbing at this point.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Good. Crash rate, Priya.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: We're at one point nine percent crash-free sessions inverted, so call it ninety-eight point one percent crash-free. Most of it is one bug in the image cache on older devices.

transcript.speaker: Luca Bertolini
transcript.text: Older meaning what?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Anything with less than three gigabytes of RAM. It's about eleven percent of our install base.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Eleven percent is too many to write off. Priya, will you own the image cache fix and land it by the thirtieth of September?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Thirtieth of September. I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Now, ship date. I had us down for the eighth of October.

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: The eighth doesn't work. If sync lands on the twenty-fourth we need at least a week of soak time with real accounts, and the eighth gives us four days.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Hm. You're right, and I'd rather hear that now. Let's move the release to the twenty-second of October. Not the eighth. Everyone note that.

transcript.speaker: Luca Bertolini
transcript.text: Twenty-second works better for me anyway, I'm out the first week of October.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Luca, that means you're on the soak-test plan. Can you write it up by the seventeenth of October?

transcript.speaker: Luca Bertolini
transcript.text: Seventeenth of October, sure. I'll circulate a draft before that.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: What about the tablet layout work? We keep pushing it.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: We're not deciding that today. Let's come back to it next week when we know how sync lands.

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: And the analytics migration? Marcus was asking.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Nobody owns that yet. I'm not assigning it in this meeting.

transcript.speaker: Luca Bertolini
transcript.text: There's also the question of whether we drop support for the oldest OS version.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Park that one. It's a bigger conversation than we have time for.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Last thing — should we run a beta programme for this release?

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Let's decide that next week as well. I don't want to half-commit to it.

transcript.speaker: Owen Brasher
transcript.text: One number for the record: our previous release took thirty-one days from code freeze to store approval. That was unusual.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Noted, but I'm not planning around thirty-one days. Anything else? No? Good, thanks everyone.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Dana, will you take the release note for the store listing? Someone has to own it.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Fine, Dana takes the store listing note. By the twentieth of October.

transcript.speaker: Luca Bertolini
transcript.text: Also Helena Fischer sent over the localisation strings, but she's not on this project any more so I just filed them.
